probability.basis: Glasgow-2462 is the proposed, very uncertain working father of the traditional Ulster ancestor Glasgow-591 and the Cavers Covenanter Glasgow-4138. This carries the existing possible identity with the Polwarth child Glasgow-1605 into a concrete local family model. The Polwarth index names the child’s father as William Glasgow, and Glasgow-2462 is already attached to that child with uncertainty. The three younger profile accounts are retained as possible stages of one life, not three proved brothers. Neither new father attachment is independent support for the other: both depend on the same child/adult identity and on the unproved identification of the named Polwarth father with the Inveresk man. The Polwarth child was baptised on 4 April 1658. If baptised near birth, he would have been about 21 at the examination of the Cavers servant in June 1679, 26 at the Ormistoun servant list in 1684 and 31 in 1689. Those are compatible ages for the recorded adult and the later military tradition. The Ulster profile’s circa 1656 birth is explicitly a rough grandson-based estimate, not an age stated by a record; its guessed Glasgow-city origin cannot exclude a Borders childhood. The exact forename and surname, compatible sequence and existing Borders candidate make this a usable provisional life model. Polwarth and Cavers are distinct parishes in different counties, and the chronology supplies compatibility rather than an identifying age match. The Cavers setting is recorded residence/association, not a proved birthplace.
